summary: Turn hotel and tour-operator CSR commitments into practical checks, indicators and action plans. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: Corporate social responsibility in tourism and hospitality helps teams turn commitments into practical, reviewable daily decisions. For hotel operations managers, tour-operator sustainability leads and procurement specialists, this includes assessing property routines, prioritizing impacts and creating workforce and supplier checks. Participants also organize CSR indicators in an Excel dashboard and map community initiatives to relevant UN Sustainable Development Goals.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for embedding social and environmental responsibility into tourism services, hotel operations, supplier decisions and destination relationships. It suits intermediate practitioners who need to coordinate CSR work across teams and present usable evidence to property or business leaders.
modules: Global Code of Ethics for Tourism in Practice
GSTC Hotel Criteria for Property Operations
OECD Due Diligence for Tourism Supply Chains
prerequisites: This intermediate course suits you if you have experience in tourism or hospitality operations, sustainability, procurement, human resources or community engagement. Familiarity with basic CSR or sustainability terminology is useful. No coding is required. Bring a laptop with Excel installed; no add-ins or external account are required.
